newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-STEVE WAUGH LEADS AUSTRALIAN RESISTANCE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-STEVE WAUGH LEADS AUSTRALIAN RESISTANCE.

text.p: An unbeaten 65 by Steve Waugh helped Australia to defy an innings defeat as they reached 232 for eight in their second innings at lunch on the fourth day of the one-off test against India on Sunday.
India had made 361 in reply to Australia's first innings total of 182.

Resuming at the overnight score of 168 for six, 11 runs in arrears of the Indian first-innings lead, Australia suffered a jolt when leg-spinner Anil Kumble had left-hander Brad Hogg caught by Vikram Rathore at forward short-leg for four.
Kumble took his second-innings haul to five wickets when he trapped Paul Reiffel leg before wicket for six with the total on 191.
But Waugh found an able ally in Peter McIntyre and the pair defied the Indian bowlers to add 41 runs in 67 minutes before lunch.
Waugh became the first Australian batsman to score 50 in the match when he square drove Kumble to the fence.
Waugh had faced 213 deliveries during his 259-minute stay at the wicket and struck five boundaries.
McIntyre's unbeaten 15 contained two boundaries from 57 balls faced.
